text: The assay office weighed its first gold in June. By September, four thousand people were living in tents along the creek. The nearest magistrate was eleven days' ride away, so for the first winter the town made its own laws and wrote them in the back of the assay ledger.
strengths: opens on an ordinary act of business
the crowd arrives as a number with a timescale
the hook is a strange document, not a promise of drama
weaknesses: the film must actually show what those laws said, or the hook is wasted
spokenRhythm: Two plain sentences that gather speed through the months, then a long one that slows down to deliver the oddity.
narrativeFunction: Opens a gold-rush film by putting its central question, how a town governs itself, inside a single account book.
whyItWorks: Nothing is called extraordinary. The speed of the rush is told through two months and one number, the isolation through one distance, and the hook is a fact so specific that the listener wants to see the ledger. Curiosity comes from the record rather than from the narrator insisting on it.

text: In the autumn of the bad harvest, the bank in the market town printed more notes than it had in the previous ten years. The increase never appeared in the half-yearly statement. Every note carried a partner's signature, and across the county people took them as readily as coin.
strengths: the bad harvest and the printing sit in one sentence and the listener joins them
the concealment is shown by what the statement leaves out, never called a secret
the last line names the trust the bank was spending and leaves the irony to work
weaknesses: relies on the next passage paying off the irony quickly
the half-yearly statement must be a document the film can show or cite
spokenRhythm: A long sentence that sets time and place, a short flat one about the books, then a steady line that ends on the county's confidence.
narrativeFunction: Opens a bank-failure story by planting the cause before anyone in the story sees the effect.
whyItWorks: The narrator never says that trouble is coming. Every sentence is a neutral fact, and the danger lives in how they sit together. The listener does the arithmetic of a bad harvest, a busy press and a quiet balance sheet, which is far more gripping than being told the bank was doomed.

text: Every boat that worked through a lock took a chamberful of water down the hill with it. At the summit of the canal, the only water came from the streams on the hills above. In a dry summer, the company had to choose between closing the canal and buying the mill owners' rights to those streams.
strengths: explains the mechanism in one plain image
each sentence adds one link in the chain
ends on a business decision rather than an engineering fact
weaknesses: assumes the film has already shown a lock working
spokenRhythm: Three sentences of similar weight that climb from a single lock to the summit and end on the company's dilemma.
narrativeFunction: Explains a hidden cost of canal building and turns it into a conflict between the canal and the mills.
whyItWorks: It explains without lecturing. There is no definition of a lock, only what each boat takes with it, and the consequence follows naturally. By the last sentence the engineering has become a choice made by people, which is where a documentary wants its explanations to land.

text: Before radio, a pilot crossing the mountains at night had a compass, a clock and a map. If he knew his speed and how long he had been in the air, he knew roughly where he was. The wind was the part of the sum he had to guess.
strengths: three tools, named once
the method explained in a single conditional sentence
the danger arrives as arithmetic
weaknesses: roughly carries a lot of weight and needs a slight stress from the voice
spokenRhythm: A short inventory, a longer if-then sentence, and a closing line that turns the explanation into a risk.
narrativeFunction: Explains dead reckoning to a general audience and sets up the danger of the night routes.
whyItWorks: The listener learns how navigation worked without a technical term. The last line is memorable because it comes out of the explanation itself, and it makes the wind the antagonist without a single dramatic word.

text: A new loom cost the mill about thirty pounds. The woman who minded it was paid twelve shillings a week. Within a year the mill had paid her more than the machine had cost, and the machine, if it was looked after, would run for twenty years.
strengths: two prices from the same mill compared directly
one number per sentence
the owner's reasoning is shown, never condemned
weaknesses: the listener has to do a little arithmetic, which is the point but asks for a pause in the edit
spokenRhythm: Two short factual sentences that set the prices, then a longer one that runs the owner's sum to its end.
narrativeFunction: Shows how a mill owner weighed people against machines, using only the mill's own figures.
whyItWorks: The money means something because it is measured against something else in the same building. There is no modern conversion and no comment on the morality. The listener works out what the owner worked out, and the conclusion is more unsettling for being left unsaid.

text: The silk in the hold was valued at four thousand ducats when the ship left port. A master shipwright in the city earned perhaps sixty in a year. The merchants who had shared the voyage would not know for eight months whether they had made a fortune or lost one.
strengths: the cargo is measured against a skilled wage in the same city
the hedge sits quietly inside the second sentence
the wait becomes part of the price
weaknesses: the ratio is left for the listener, which some viewers will not compute
spokenRhythm: A long sentence for the cargo, a shorter one for the wage, then a long line that ends on a neat turn.
narrativeFunction: Establishes the scale of a trading venture and the uncertainty the merchants lived with.
whyItWorks: Four thousand ducats is meaningless alone and vivid next to a shipwright's year. The last sentence adds time to money, which is what made the trade frightening, and the closing phrase is neat without becoming a slogan.

text: Elias Brand kept the harbour board's accounts for thirty-one years, and as far as the books show, he never once made a mistake in addition. He made other kinds. The first was lending the board his own savings.
strengths: the character is drawn from what the records show
a three-word sentence turns praise into foreshadowing
the humour is dry and kind
weaknesses: a turn this neat can be used only once in a film
spokenRhythm: A long admiring sentence, a very short one that tips it over, and a medium line that names the first mistake.
narrativeFunction: Introduces a minor figure whose loyalty will drive the plot, and hints at his fate without announcing it.
whyItWorks: The introduction is built from evidence, not adjectives. He made other kinds is short, surprising and dry, and it arises from the story rather than from a writer reaching for a line. The listener likes him and worries for him in the same breath.

text: When the ship sailed, Hannah Reed's husband would be gone for three years, perhaps four. In that time she ran the chandlery, sued two of its debtors and bought a share in another ship. His letters, when they reached her, mostly asked for her advice.
strengths: three actions say more than any description of her
the husband's letters reverse the expected roles quietly
no comment on how unusual she was
weaknesses: the claim about the letters must rest on letters the production can actually cite
spokenRhythm: A sentence with a hedge in its tail, a brisk list of three deeds, then a gentle line with a pause in the middle.
narrativeFunction: Introduces a woman who ran a whaling family's business and establishes who really held the power.
whyItWorks: The narrator never tells us she was capable or ahead of her time. Her actions do it, and the last line lets her husband confirm it. The humour is in the detail, and the listener gets to notice it.

text: The story goes that the town's first coffee house was opened by a sailor who had learned the trade in the eastern ports. It's a good story, and the town still tells it. The earliest record of coffee being sold there is a licence granted to a widow, for a shop that also sold tobacco and candles.
strengths: the legend is told fairly before the record is set beside it
no announcement that the legend is false
the humble detail of tobacco and candles does the deflating
weaknesses: the earliest record is not proof the sailor never existed, and the film should not imply that it is
spokenRhythm: A long legend, a short warm aside, then a long plain sentence that ends on ordinary goods.
narrativeFunction: Separates a town's favourite origin story from what the documents actually show.
whyItWorks: Uncertainty is handled the way a curious person would handle it, with respect for the story and interest in the paperwork. There is no disclaimer and no claim of a hidden truth, only a second account that is less romantic and better documented.

text: The expedition's map shows a lake about twenty miles west of the river. Nobody has found it since. The surveyor may have seen a valley in flood, or he may have drawn in a lake that someone at the trading post described to him. His notebook for that fortnight is missing, which doesn't help.
strengths: two explanations offered, neither forced
the gap in the source is named plainly
the dry close keeps the tone light
weaknesses: which doesn't help is a quip the film can afford only once
spokenRhythm: A plain statement, a short flat reply, a long sentence weighing two possibilities, and a dry tail.
narrativeFunction: Turns a mapping error into a small investigation and shows how the evidence runs out.
whyItWorks: The narrator is openly unsure and openly interested. The possibilities are reasonable, the missing notebook is a real limit, and the closing aside sounds like a person rather than a disclaimer. Nothing is shrouded and nothing is promised.

text: The quarantine lasted forty days, and the ship's cotton sat in the lazaretto for every one of them. By the time it was released, the price in the city had fallen by a quarter. The merchant who owned it spent the next two years in court, trying to make the health board pay the difference.
strengths: the epidemic story hands over to a legal story through one cargo
one number per sentence
the merchant enters as a consequence, not an announcement
weaknesses: lazaretto may need a picture or an earlier line to be understood
spokenRhythm: A long sentence that sits through the quarantine, a shorter one for the fall in price, then the longest, which carries the story from the harbour into the courtroom.
narrativeFunction: Moves the film from public health to its cost for trade, and introduces the litigant who carries the next section.
whyItWorks: The turn is made by following the cotton. Quarantine causes delay, delay costs money, and money produces a lawsuit. No signpost is needed because each sentence is the consequence of the one before.

text: The company's first timetable allowed four hours for the run to the coast. A decade later, the same journey took two. The fishing town at the end of the line had started letting rooms by the week, mostly to clerks from the city and their families.
strengths: a decade passes in a short sentence
the social change is shown through one ordinary arrangement
the new visitors are named precisely
weaknesses: the link between faster trains and the lodging trade is implied rather than proved
spokenRhythm: A medium sentence, a short one that jumps the years, then a longer line that lands the change.
narrativeFunction: Carries the railway story from engineering into its effect on a seaside town.
whyItWorks: There is no line saying the town would never be the same. The timetable shrinks, and the town starts doing something new, and the listener connects them. The clerks give the change a face without a speech about the rise of leisure.

text: The new shaft took four winters to sink. The men were paid by the foot, so a week of flooding was a week without wages. The pay book lists them by name for the first winter. By the third, most of them are listed by number.
strengths: the narration carries pay and turnover, which no picture of a shaft can show
names giving way to numbers implies the turnover without stating it
no word about suffering
weaknesses: the closing line works best over a held shot and needs room in the edit
spokenRhythm: A short statement, a longer sentence of cause and effect, then two shorter lines that fall quietly.
narrativeFunction: Gives a mining scene its human cost while the pictures show the shaft and the landscape.
whyItWorks: The images can show the hill and the headgear. The narration supplies what only the records know, how the men were paid and how many of them came and went. The final line lets a clerk's bookkeeping say what the narrator never states.

text: The committee had decided that the grain would be sold at cost, because it believed free food would ruin the town's bakers. Families with nothing left to sell went past the warehouse every day. It stayed full until May.
strengths: the committee's reasoning is given fairly before its result
no adjective tells the listener what to feel
a short last line carries the weight
weaknesses: the committee's belief should come from its own minutes, not the writer's summary
spokenRhythm: A long sentence of policy, a medium one of people, and a five-word ending.
narrativeFunction: Sets a relief scene in the gap between a policy and the people it was meant to help.
whyItWorks: The narration explains why the decision was made, then simply places hungry families beside a full warehouse. The listener supplies the anger. The house never needs to say it was a tragedy when the arrangement of facts already says so.

text: The insurance company failed in its ninth year. Its policyholders got back a little under a third of what they were owed, and the last resolution in the minute book is to sell the office furniture. Most of the ships it had insured were still at sea.
strengths: the failure is recorded in the company's own last act
the final line opens a new worry without a tease
no moral is drawn
weaknesses: needs the film to have explained what a policy protected, or the last line loses its weight
spokenRhythm: A short opening, a long sentence of aftermath, and a quiet closing line that lingers.
narrativeFunction: Closes the story of an underwriting firm by leaving its risks still sailing.
whyItWorks: The ending is made of facts. The office furniture is a small, dry detail, and the ships still at sea give the listener something to think about after the voice stops. It resonates without trailer language and without explaining what it means.

text: The harbour silted up over about two centuries. No council ever voted to abandon the city. Each year a few more families left for the coast, and each year the ones who stayed had a little further to walk to the sea.
strengths: two centuries told through one daily walk
the slow decline is described at the speed it happened
the image grows out of the geography, not decoration
weaknesses: the parallel in the last sentence is a device the film should not repeat elsewhere
spokenRhythm: Two short plain sentences, then a long one whose repetition slows the voice like the silt it describes.
narrativeFunction: Ends the story of an ancient port by making its decline gradual, human and physical.
whyItWorks: There is no fall, no doom and no lesson. The city empties the way it really would have, one household at a time, and the last line is memorable because it is literally true. A listener could repeat it to a friend.
